questions.question: In a certain code language, "BAPTISM​​" is written as "DCRVKUO​". How is "TIN" written in that code language?
questions.solution:
The word BAPTISM is coded as:

B + 2 = D

A + 2 = C

P + 2 = R

T + 2 = V

I + 2 = K

S + 2 = U

M + 2 = O

Same pattern will be followed to answer the question:

T + 2 = V

I + 2 = K

N + 2 = P

Hence, TIN will be coded as VKP.

questions.question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

1, 0.25, 1/9, ?, 0.04, 1/36​
questions.solution:
Numbers are written in the form of ‘1/n²’.

1/1² = 1

1/2² = 1/4 = 0.25

1/3² = 1/9

**1/4² = 1/16 = 0.0625**

1/5² = 1/25 = 0.04

1/6² = 1/36

Hence, the missing term is 0.0625.

questions.question: Eshan's birthday is on Friday 10th March. On what day of the week will be Shlok's Birthday in the same year if Shlok was born on 25th September?
questions.solution:
According to the question, 10th March is Friday.

Number of days left in March = 31 – 10 = 21.

Similarly, odd days from 10th March till 25th September = (21 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 25) % 7 = 0 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 4 = 17/7.

Remainder = 3.

Thus, day on 25th September = Friday (+3) = Monday.

Hence, Shlok's birthday will be on Monday.

questions.question:
In the question, a statement is given, followed by two arguments, I and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given arguments, if any, is a strong argument.

**Statement:** Should zoos be closed down?

**Argument**** I:** Yes, imprisoning animals is unethical.

**Argument II:** No, it is fine if some animals are kept in captivity for sake of entertainment.

options.text: Both I and II are strong.
Neither I nor II is strong.

questions.solution:
The statement questions whether or not the zoos should be closed. From the given two statements under arguments, the first one states that the zoos must be closed as they are the representation of animal-imprisonment, which is correct, therefore, it suggests that the first argument is strong. 

The second argument negates the previous one by stating that the animals must be used for the sake of entertainment. This argument is weak as zoos do not necessarily captivate animals for entertainment, but at times for education use as well. In addition, treating animals for entertainment makes this argument weak.

Therefore, only argument I is strong. Answer is option (1).

questions.question: What type of a body plan does coelenterates, ctenophores and echinoderms have?
questions.solution: Animals can be categorized on the basis of their symmetry. When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called **radial symmetry**. Coelenterates, Ctenophores and Echinoderms have this kind of body plan.

questions.question: Lion, Leopard and Tiger are all species of which genus?
questions.solution: Lion, Leopard and Tiger are all species of the genus Panthera. Panthera is a genus within the *Felidae* family that was named and first described by the German naturalist Oken in 1816. The British taxonomist Pocock revised the classification of this genus in 1916 as comprising the species lion, tiger, *jaguar**,* and leopard on the basis of cranial features.

questions.question: ________ means that the President of India can refer any matter that is of public importance or that which involves interpretation of Constitution to Supreme Court for advice.
questions.solution: Article 143 of the Indian Constitution confers upon the Supreme Court advisory jurisdiction. The President may seek the opinion of the Supreme Court on any question of law or fact of public importance on which he thinks it beneficial to obtain such an opinion. On such reference from the President, the Supreme Court, after giving it such hearing as it deems fit, may report to the President its opinion thereon. The opinion is only advisory, which the President is free to follow or not to follow.

questions.question: ___________ is the set of all possible combinations of the two inputs that yield the same maximum possible level of output.
questions.solution: An *isoquant* traces out the *combinations* of any *two* *inputs* which *yield* *the same level of output*. An *isoquant* expresses the *set* of technically efficient processes that *yield the same output*. On the basis of the substitutability of *inputs* it is a curve that illustrates *all possible combinations* of resources that will produce a particular *level of output*.

questions.question: If the speed of an object moving along a straight line is constant, its motion is said to be _________.
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Speed (v): The rate of change of distance is called Speed.

 
 
• Speed = Distance/ Time.
 
• Its unit is m/s or km/hr
 
 
 
• Uniform Speed: The motion in which a body is moving with a constant speed (no acceleration) is called uniform speed motion.
 
• Odometer or odograph: It is a device used to measure the distance travelled by the vehicle.
 
• Speedometer or speed meter: A device used by the vehicle to measure the speed of the vehicle

Explanation:__

__
 
• Uniform motion is defined as the motion of an object in which the object travels in a straight line.
 
• Its velocity remains constant along that line as it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, irrespective of the length of the time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Uniform motion: when an object covers equal distance in the equal time interval of time said to be in uniform motion. Here acceleration is zero.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f888266b06d61365f214addeb6a62a20447697e65f76a78034aa04ae8776083.png] 

 
• Non-Uniform motion: when an object covers unequal distances in the equal time interval of time said to be in non-uniform motion. Here acceleration is non- zero.

questions.question: __________ are made up of sclerenchymatous cells. These are generally absent in the primary phloem but are found in the secondary phloem.

questions.question: The sum of a fraction and 3 times its reciprocal is 37/10. What is the fraction?
questions.solution:
Let the fraction be y

According to the problem statement

⇒ y + 3/y = 37/10

⇒ 10y² – 37y + 30 = 0

⇒ (y – 5/2) (y – 6/5) = 0

⇒ y = 5/2 or y = 6/5

Only 5/2 satisfies the required condition given in the question

∴ the fraction is 5/2

⇒ Sec θ = √(1 + 7²/24²)

⇒ Sec θ = √{(576 + 49)/24²}

⇒ Sec θ = √{(25²)/24²} = 25/24

∴ Sec θ = 25/24

questions.question: If compound interest received on a certain amount in the 2ⁿd year is Rs. 1200, what will be the compound interest (in Rs.) for the 4th year on the same amount at 10% rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Let the amount be Rs. y

Compound interest for 2ⁿd year can be given as

⇒ CI for 2ⁿd year = y{(1 + 10/100)² – (1 + 10/100)} = 1200

⇒ 1200 = y(1.1² – 1.1)

⇒ 1200/0.11 = y

⇒ y = Rs. 10909.1

Compound interest for 4th year can be given as

⇒ CI for 4th year = y{(1 + 10/100)⁴ – (1 + 10/100)³}

⇒ CI for 4th year = 10909.1(1.1⁴ – 1.1³) = 10909.1 × 0.1331

⇒ CI for 4th year = Rs. 1452

∴ Interest for 4th year is Rs. 1452

questions.question: The 4th and 7th term of an arithmetic progression are 11 and - 4 respectively. What is the 15th term?
questions.solution:
Let the first term of AP be a and common difference be d

From the problem’s statement

⇒ 4th term = a + (4 - 1)d = a + 3d = 11 ---- (i)

⇒ 7th term = a + (7 - 1)d = a + 6d = - 4 ---- (ii)

Now (ii) - (i)

⇒ 3d = -15

⇒ d = - 5, put this in (i)

⇒ a = 11 + 15 = 26

Now the 15th term can be given as a + 14d

⇒ 16th term = 26 + 14 × (-5) = - 44

∴ The 15th term of AP is – 44

questions.question: What is the reflection of the point (5, -1) in the line y = 2?
questions.solution:
Reflection of point about y = 2 can be given as

Since we know that the X co-ordinate will not change

And the y co-ordinate can be given as given

y co-ordinate + 2 × (y co-ordinate of line – given y co-ordinate)

⇒ -1 + 2 × (2 – (-1)) = 5

∴ the co-ordinate of reflection is (5, 5)

questions.question: A, B and C can finish a job working alone in 20, 30 and 60 days respectively. They all work together for 1 day, then A and B quit. How many days C working alone will take to finish the remaining part of the job?
questions.solution:
Work done by A in 1 day can be given as 1/20th of the total work

Work done by B in 1 day can be given as 1/30th of the total work

Work done by C in 1 day can be given as 1/60th of the total work

Let the number of days for which C have to work alone be y

According to the problem statement

⇒ 1(1/20 + 1/30 + 1/60) + y(1/60) = 1

⇒ y/60 = 1 – 1/10

⇒ y = 54 days

∴ the number of days required to complete the remaining work by C is 54

questions.question: If 3A = 2B = 4C; then what is A ∶ B ∶ C?
questions.solution:
Using first two equations

⇒ 3A = 2B

⇒ B = 3A/2 ----(i)

Using first and third equation

⇒ 3A = 4C

⇒ C = 3A/4 ----(ii)

Required ratio is A ∶ B ∶ C, Using (i) and (ii)

Required ratio A ∶ 3A/2 ∶ 3A/4

Required ratio = 4 ∶ 6 ∶ 3

∴ The required ratio is 4 ∶ 6 ∶ 3

questions.question: The average cost of 5 items in a shopping list is Rs. 650. If one more item whose cost is Rs. 1400 is added to the list what will be the new average (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Average cost of 5 items is given as Rs. 650

⇒ sum of cost of 5 items/5 = 650

⇒ sum of cost of 5 items = 5 × 650 = 3250 ----(i)

Average cost of 6 items can be given as

⇒ Average = (sum of cost of 5 items + 1400)/6 [Using (i)]

⇒ Average = (3250 + 1400)/6 = 775

∴ The new average is Rs. 775

questions.question: If the selling price of an item is Rs. 9750 after getting a discount of 25%, then what was its marked price (in Rs.)?

⇒ y = 9750/0.75

⇒ y = 13000

questions.question: If fees charged by the coaching centre was Rs. 10000 for the first 3 years and Rs. 12000 for the next three years then what is the total fees (in Rs. Crores) collected by the coaching centre in the last six years?
questions.solution:
Total number of students in first 3 years can be given as

Total number of students = 100 + 150 + 150 = 400

Fees collected by them = 400 × 10000 = Rs. 4000000

Total number of students in last 3 years can be given as

Total number of students = 250 + 350 + 300 = 900

Fees collected by them = 900 × 12000 = Rs. 10800000

Total fee = 4000000 + 10800000 = Rs. 1.48 crore
